transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aaron Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Veridian Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Veridian Platform Eng), Sanjay Patel (Veridian Security), Evan Brooks (Veridian CTO)

Summary (auto): Discussed reliability and incident tolerance requirements; explored Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options; reviewed fallback strategies, multi-region routing, and SLA targets. Agreed on pilot/benchmark next steps.

00:00 Aaron: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros?
00:07 Marta: Hi, Marta Ruiz here, I lead the ML platform at Veridian.
00:10 Liam: Liam O'Connor, platform eng, we'll be owning infra for any integration.
00:13 Sanjay: Sanjay, security. We'll need to validate compliance.
00:16 Aaron: Great. Priya, pitch?
00:18 Priya: Hi all, Priya Shah, solutions engineering at Redwood. Today we'll focus on reliability, incident tolerance, fallbacks, and what Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private look like operationally.
00:30 Aaron: High level, Veridian told us you have a customer-facing recommendation engine, tight p95 latency targets, and hard uptime needs. Confirm?
00:35 Marta: Yeah, our rec engine drives conversions. p95 needs to be under 220ms for interactive flows, but batch scoring can be slower. Uptime, we need five 9s internally but we know customer-facing features are negotiated.
00:47 Evan: Also, we have a global footprint, need multi-region support for EU and NA, potential APAC later.
00:52 Priya: Good context. A couple of core patterns we'll propose: primary region serving with automated region failover, model variant fallback (e.g., smaller quantized model) for latency spikes, and reserved Dedicated pools for steady-state throughput.
01:05 Liam: Model fallback sounds interesting. How does that work with state like KV caches and context?
01:12 Priya: Good question. Our runtime keeps KV cache warm for active sessions. When we fallback to a different model family we flush or transform KV cache depending on compatibility - for compatible variants we reuse cache, for incompatible we have a short degraded state while we rebuild. That can add a few 100s ms for a small percentage of requests.
01:28 Marta: A few hundred milliseconds could kill conversions. Is there a way to do edge-caching or prefix caching to avoid that hit?
01:34 Priya: We recommend prefix/KV caching at the request layer - so for commonly repeated prefixes we serve from cache. Also, canary routing: route a small percentage to fallback model ahead of failures to warm cache.
01:50 Aaron: Note, some transcriptions say canary as 'kaniary' - ignore.
01:55 Sanjay: From security side, how do you guarantee data residency and encryption in multi-region setup?
02:01 Priya: For Hosted we offer region-specific endpoints and can restrict where data is stored; Dedicated and Private give you more control - Private supports VPC-only control plane and on-prem options. All modes support customer-managed KMS for key control.
02:15 Sanjay: KMS + HSM details we'll need. Also SSO and SAML for operator access.
02:21 Aaron: We'll share our security pack - SOC 2, ISO, KMS integration docs, and network diagrams.
02:26 Marta: Thanks. SLA question: what's the SLA for Hosted vs Dedicated?
02:31 Priya: Hosted has an uptime SLO with best-effort SLAs in early tiers; Dedicated comes with contractual SLA - 99.95% is typical for reserved capacity plans, with latency objectives per model family, and Private can have bespoke SLA with account execs.
02:47 Liam: If a region goes down, what's typical failover time? And do you handle DNS and traffic shift?
02:55 Priya: We have two main strategies: active-active multi-region (preferred for low RTO) where traffic is routed at our edge and we do health-based load balancing, or active-passive where we failover to a secondary region. For active-active, failover is near-instant for new requests if caches are primed. For active-passive, depending on DNS TTL and BGP reconvergence, you're looking at 30s to a few minutes unless you use our edge-based routing which is faster.
03:23 Marta: For near-zero RTO we probably need active-active. Cost implications?
03:29 Priya: Active-active increases duplication of reserves and cache warmers - roughly 1.6x-2x cost depending on utilization, but reduces cold starts and cache misses. We can recommend autoscaling and warm standby policies to balance that.
03:42 Aaron: One thing customers ask: fallback to cheaper model vs returning an error. What's Redwood's default?
03:48 Priya: Default is smart fallback to a compatible variant - we first try a smaller quantized model in the same family, then broader fallback to a cheaper family if configured. You can also set strict mode to fail closed.
03:59 Liam: How do you measure fidelity loss when falling back? We need guardrails so business SLAs don't degrade.
04:05 Priya: We tie fallbacks to evals and golden prompt sets. We can set thresholds on recovery metrics (score drop) and only allow fallback if quality delta is within tolerance. These are configurable per route.
04:20 Marta: Excellent. About observability - what traces and token-level metrics do you provide?
04:26 Priya: Token-level cost and latency, per-request traces, KV cache hit ratios, model variant mapping per request, and sampling for outputs. Console shows trace links, and we integrate with OpenTelemetry traces through a tracing hook.
04:40 Sanjay: Audit logs for admin actions and keys rotation?
04:44 Priya: Yes, audit logs are available for Dedicated/Private with retention options; Hosted has standard retention but enterprise add-on for longer retention.
04:54 Evan: Any customers running on hybrid-like Dedicated for NA and Private for EU?
04:58 Aaron: We do see hybrid setups. Redwood's routing supports policy-based routing by region, cost tier, or legal constraints.
05:06 Marta: On the technical side, what's the KV cache size behavior across regions? If we replicate caches, that's more memory.
05:12 Priya: We avoid full replication for large KV caches. Our common pattern is a hot set replication and lazy fetch for cold keys; replication policy is configurable.
05:22 Liam: For the pilot, we'd like to simulate a region outage and observe fallback. Can you support a scheduled chaos window?
05:30 Priya: Yes, in Dedicated/Private we can coordinate a controlled failover test; for Hosted we provide a sandbox with simulated failures.
05:38 Aaron: Let's talk about pricing sensitivity - Veridian prefers predictable cost. Dedicated reserved capacity helps.
05:44 Marta: We want unit economics: cost per 1k requests at our 220ms p95. Can you model that?
05:49 Priya: We'll run your traffic profile against a couple of model configs; that's what the benchmark spreadsheet will do. We'll include active-active vs active-passive cost estimates, fallback hit rates, and cache warming overhead.
06:01 Sanjay: Legal question: in the event of incident, do you provide post-mortem and root cause analysis?
06:06 Priya: Yes, enterprise customers get incident reports, timeline, and mitigation notes. We also support runbook integration and can provide push notifications to your on-call systems.
06:18 Marta: Excellent. A few nitty-gritty items: are model weights ever stored outside a customer region for Dedicated?
06:24 Priya: For Dedicated with region pinning, weights and inference artifacts can be restricted. For Hosted default, weights may be in multiple regions for availability but request data residency can be enforced. For Private we can keep everything on-prem.
06:39 Liam: On networking: do you do private inter-region peering?
06:42 Priya: For Dedicated we can do private peering between Redwood-managed clusters; for Private you'll set up your own networking.
06:49 Marta: We have a constraint: no egress of raw input data to third-party regions. Can Redwood meet that?
06:55 Priya: Yes with region locking and VPC-private routing, we can restrict egress - that's a typical enterprise requirement.
07:02 Aaron: Quick aside, some transcription engine swapped 'KV cache' to 'K V cake' earlier - ignore.
07:07 Sanjay: About encryption at rest for embeddings and logs?
07:11 Priya: We encrypt at rest with customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private; Hosted supports customer KMS in enterprise tiers. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
07:20 Evan: For SLA penalties, typical arrangements?
07:24 Priya: Standard credit model tied to uptime buckets. For Dedicated contract we negotiate specific terms. We'll include sample SLA language in the docs.
07:33 Marta: Ok, recapping what we need: pricing + capacity models, security docs, benchmark run, and a scheduled failover test.
07:41 Aaron: Yep. We'll action those.
07:44 Priya: Technical deep dive can focus on caching, canary strategies, and quantization impact on latency/quality.
07:51 Liam: One more - how do rollouts work for model updates? Do you support gradual canary and automatic rollback?
07:57 Priya: Yes, rollouts support canary percentages, automatic rollback on error or quality regressions, and A/B tests. We also have automatic fallback if a new model exceeds error thresholds.
08:11 Marta: Perfect. Any blockers from security?
08:14 Sanjay: Need SOC2, KMS/HSM integration details, and network diagrams.
08:19 Aaron: We'll send all those in the security pack.
08:22 Priya: Also we'll include a sample runbook for chaos testing and can coordinate a pilot window.
08:28 Evan: Timeline: we'd like to decide whether to proceed with Dedicated vs Hosted by end of Q3. Pilot in August.
08:34 Aaron: Sounds doable. We'll aim to have pricing + docs early August.
08:37 Priya: Any other questions?
08:39 Marta: Not at the moment.
08:41 Liam: None.
08:43 Sanjay: None.
08:44 Aaron: Great - recap of next steps then.
